params.name: Act on
params.tooltip:
Which towns get new streets in their region's style. New
towns only: towns founded after the mod was added to this
save (on a new map, every town). All towns: existing towns
too. Off: the mod does nothing.

params.name: Vanilla town street angles
params.tooltip:
Sets the game's own street angles for town layouts, by the
map's region: Automatic picks straight grids for North
America and Oceania, irregular streets for Europe and the
Mediterranean. Applies to new towns (a new map's starting
towns) and to the game's own street growth, not when Act on
is Off. Existing saves: only towns founded later and later
growth. Game default: no change.

params.name: Starting town size
params.tooltip:
Shrinks the towns the map generator places on a new map, so
the head start and growth have room to shape each town.
Smaller: x0.6, Small: x0.35 of the game's Population setting.
A test: it may lower only the residents, not the streets.
Pick it when you create a new map; keep Game size on an
existing save. Game size: no change.

params.name: Streets at industries
params.tooltip:
Off: a new map's industries get none of the small streets the
map generator lays at their edge, so towns don't fill them with
a cluster of houses next to the works. Game default: the game's
streets. Only affects new maps; an existing save keeps its streets.

params.name: Town and stop names
params.tooltip:
Landscape names: on a new map every town gets a new name
made up from its region, climate and map: the name list's
language with the town's coast, river, hills and trees
(palms and reefs in the tropics, birch and fells in the
north). Rivers and lakes are named too, satellite towns
fit their site. New road stops get a street name that
fits their spot. Game names: the game's names. Lists without
a generator (Asian, Chinese, Korean, Polish, Russian) keep
the game's names. Towns of older saves are never renamed.
Towns on a name list from another mod keep their names; new
satellite towns are named in that list's language.

params.name: Town growth
params.tooltip:
By deliveries: each town's mix of residential, commercial and
industrial follows what you deliver, so towns can grow clearly
lopsided: a town fed with industrial cargo grows mostly
industry, one served only by passenger lines mostly homes.
It changes the mix as the town grows, not how fast it grows.
Follows Act on. Removing the mod keeps the towns as they are.
How strongly: the Delivery weighting setting.
Game default: the game evens each town's mix out.

params.name: Delivery weighting
params.tooltip:
How strongly deliveries steer each town's mix when Town growth
is By deliveries. Full: towns follow your deliveries closely
(mill towns, commuter towns). Light: towns stay close to an
even mix. Medium (the default): the middle ground.
A save loaded with another weighting turns its towns slowly,
with their growth; nothing is torn down. Saves from before
this setting use Medium too.

params.name: Satellite towns
params.tooltip:
On a new map some grown towns found small separate towns nearby,
one at a time and spread over the years: residential districts
and industrial Works, linked by a road. They only grow further
when you serve them with transport. Off: none are founded; towns
founded already stay as they are.

params.name: Strong town characters
params.tooltip:
On a new map 1-3 towns on a striking site get a strong character:
a hilltop village, a clifftop strip, a harbor cove, a riverside
town, a street village, a company town, a garden city, an island
town, or a new town with roundabouts (needs Roundabouts &
Interchanges). About a third of the towns build up their center
once grown. Off: none of this; deep forest towns stay as they are.

params.name: Town style
params.tooltip:
Automatic: the towns' look follows the map's name list.
Pick a region to choose it apart from the names, e.g. US
names with European organic towns. Each town still fits its
style to its site within the region's mix: flat open land
grows grids and suburbs; coasts, hills and valleys denser,
winding streets. The climate adds its own bias. North
American grid: every town grows a grid. Mixed: all regions
alike. Town names always follow the name list.
With Roundabouts & Interchanges, towns also build some one-way
roundabouts from about 1960 (none in dense Japanese towns).
Name lists from other mods are recognized by their
file names (e.g. german, deutsch), else the climate decides.

params.name: Town layout
params.tooltip:
How organic or gridded towns are laid out. Organic: winding
streets, gridded towns and districts stay a minority and grow
more common in later years. Gridded: more planned grid towns
and straighter outer districts. Old town centers keep their
streets; it applies to new towns and new outer districts.

params.name: Growth lookahead
params.tooltip:
How far ahead of demand towns get new streets. Small: a few
blocks just before the free lots run out. Large: bigger
increments, earlier.

params.name: Debug log
params.tooltip:
Off: normal play. On: Organic Towns writes every town check
and planning step to the game's log file (stdout.txt, lines
starting with [SQOT]). Builds are always logged.
